title: Stabilize session handoff orchestration
summary: Closed after implementation pass, clean local publisher proof, archive ref, and task-close validation pass.

goal.outcome: CodeWiki handoff orchestration is recoverable and adapter-managed: no user-facing handoff command burden, no hidden compaction result loss, clear fresh-session semantics, and artifact waiters have a wake/resume path.
acceptance: Accepted handoff recovery feedback build is preserved and linked in task evidence.
Pi handoff behavior is grounded in current Pi docs/examples/API, including `ctx.newSession`, `withSession`, `sendUserMessage`, compaction, and session replacement limits.
Context-reset handoffs do not auto-queue immediate compaction from tool context and preserve visible tool results.
New-session handoffs either use `ctx.newSession({ withSession })` safely inside command context or a documented fallback when true new terminal tab/process is not available through Pi extension APIs.
The handoff command is no longer required as a user-facing recovery step; tool/adapter behavior must hide or internalize it where possible, with explicit fallback only when Pi API cannot do more.
Artifact wait/release records enough ready/wake evidence for waiting sessions to discover and resume when blockers release, without busy polling or hidden user commands.
KB/API docs define required handoff points and when to use fresh session, context reset, external orchestrator, or no handoff.
A CodeWiki worktree factory or orchestration path can prepare, record, heartbeat, verify, and clean task/role worktrees with path, branch, base/head/tree SHA, clean-state, and digest metadata.
Artifact status and generated state expose exact worktree/branch/patch/claim blockers and next safe actions for wait/wake records instead of vague dirty-root blockers.
Implementation validation can verify builder refs from a fresh validator worktree, while task-close/publication requires a publisher result with clean immutable proof.

A publisher/merge queue or equivalent serialized publisher path can consume a validated branch/patch ref, refresh generated CodeWiki state, produce final commit/tree proof, and update task-close readiness evidence.
Smoke tests cover worktree metadata, wait/wake blocker wording, publisher-proof gating, and shared-dirty-root non-blocking behavior for isolated refs.
non_goals: Do not resume TASK-001 until handoff blocker path is stable enough for validation/implementation loops.
Do not claim terminal-tab support unless Pi exposes an API or safe external process path is implemented.
Do not weaken CodeWiki traceability, artifact status, or fresh validation requirements.
Do not remove or extract /wiki-session-handoff compatibility command in this task; schedule that cleanup after this path is validated.
Do not weaken fresh validation, task-close, publication, or GC archive proof requirements.
Do not implement remote push/release automation beyond local proof needed for task-close readiness.
Do not make artifact status records the filesystem source of truth.
verification: Run CodeWiki alignment, stale-reference, generated-parity, file-structure, and changed audits.
Run focused smoke tests for role worktree isolation, artifact status wait/wake, session handoff, and validation proof gating.
Run CodeWiki alignment, changed, stale-reference, generated-parity, file-structure, and package audits.

delta.desired:
Session handoff becomes adapter-managed, visibly recoverable, policy-defined, and coordinated with artifact wait/release state.
Refinement: Additional outcome: Builder, validator, and publisher roles can operate through isolated task/role worktrees or refs, and task-close/publication can use a serialized publisher result instead of waiting on unrelated shared-root dirty state.
Refinement: Parallel write sessions use isolated role worktrees/refs and a publisher queue for final clean proof.
delta.current:
Multiple sessions can block around /wiki-session-handoff: fresh sessions are not new terminal tabs, context-reset can hide tool results, artifact waiters lack wake communication, and handoff remains user-facing.
Refinement: Parallel write sessions can still block on unrelated shared-root dirty state despite artifact status metadata.

title: Consolidate agent workflow surface and automate session boundaries
summary: Closed after implementation pass, clean local publisher proof, archive ref, and task-close validation pass.

goal.outcome: CodeWiki exposes a smaller direct workflow surface and required session/context boundaries are handled by the agent/adapter without asking the user to paste or press Enter on internal compatibility commands.
acceptance: `codewiki_claim` is not registered and callers use `codewiki_artifact_status` directly.
Static application tool catalog source is removed; the skill-facing catalog remains the documented tool map.
Deleted alias/catalog files are absent from package smoke and active docs.
Artifact-status coordination tests cover mark/read-overlap/conflict/release without the claim alias.
Active system docs and roadmap no longer instruct preserving wrapper aliases as the migration policy.
Session-boundary flow does not present /wiki-session-handoff or equivalent compatibility commands as normal user work for required boundaries.
Where Pi/adapter APIs can execute a boundary automatically, CodeWiki does so from agent-owned control flow and restarts from CodeWiki refs.

Where host APIs cannot execute a boundary from tool context, CodeWiki records an explicit platform limitation/fallback with next safe action instead of asking the user to press Enter as a routine step.
Workflow-efficiency evidence records user-interrupt/manual-command impact for the session-boundary path and keeps validation/task-close/publication proof gates intact.
Focused smoke tests cover automatic/no-user-command behavior and unsupported fallback semantics.
non_goals: Do not remove real application use-case services that still orchestrate IO, mutation, rebuild, or validation.
Do not refactor `src/application/claims.ts` into domain in this slice; keep runtime coordination behavior stable while removing the public alias.
Do not reopen TASK-006 role-worktree/publisher proof semantics except where session-boundary UX/tool surface needs stale-reference cleanup.
Do not implement full decision_build compiler in this task.
Do not weaken fresh-context/content-proof requirements for validation, task-close, publication, publish, or release.
Do not promise true new terminal/tab/process creation when Pi does not expose it; use explicit external-orchestrator/worker fallback language when needed.
Do not make completion-report generation the primary deliverable; keep it as follow-on unless small integration is needed for efficiency evidence.
verification: Run tests/smoke/session-handoff.test.mjs and related claim/wait smoke tests.
Run CodeWiki audits: alignment, changed, stale-reference, file-structure, generated-parity.
Validate implementation from fresh CodeWiki refs with checked content proof.

delta.desired: Deprecated tool aliases and dead application catalog are gone; replacement surfaces are direct; required new_session/context_refresh boundaries are agent-owned and no routine user command/Enter is needed.
delta.current: Claim alias/catalog cleanup is in progress, but session-boundary flow still has compatibility-command/editor-prefill/platform-fallback friction that feels slower than plain agent coding.

Existing public tool behavior and generated artifact shapes remain compatible.

relevant smoke tests if the baseline runner can execute
